about: The ADR-187 divergence ledger for SCALPEL (ADR-187 §5, started by ADR-189 / B355). Every intentional difference between the parity target (the composed engine) and an oracle it calls (the SCALPEL oracle; since B382 also SwarmSynth, reference/swarmsaw.html), one entry each; the order of the entries carries no meaning. A built entry sits behind its own engine flag, default 0 unless the entry says `default: 1` (B382, ADR-187 A1: a divergence the human ruled ON, one per PR; it carries `ruled`, and `moves` for each pinned scenario it changes at the defaults), so all flags off is the engine before the first divergence, bit for bit. Checked by tools/labharness/divergence_ledger_check.mjs (./verify fast): L1 shape, L2 the oracle blob, L3 each built flag exists at its ledgered default, L4 all off = the pinned fingerprints below and the defaults = the pins or the claimed moves, L5 each built flag changes a scenario, L6 each stays in its declared scope, L7 the engine's SwarmSynth patches and their entries are one set, L8 every divergence flag the engine has is a built entry's, L9 the entries' order changes no finding. A scope scenario is a preset name, or {preset, over, sr}, or that with a note `script` ("on <note>...", "off <note>...", "render <samples>"; B465) for a divergence that acts on event timing. Mirror policy (ADR-187, ratified): the composed engine IS the lab JS, so these are mirrored by construction; js_limit states what the browser cannot follow, or null.

divergences.description: First-order ADAA on a blade carrier, REPLACING the scanner's carrier-wrap PolyBLEPs, NARROWED by ADR-189 A1 to where it beats them: the carrier shape is not sine (nor sine->saw, which has no antiderivative), AND (the blade is an FM mode, 1 or 2, OR Band-limit is off), AND an FM blade's modulator is not S&H (mshape 7). Discrete per-blade parameters, no thresholds. Everywhere else the carrier keeps its BLEPs, bit for bit. The carrier sample becomes its mean over the phase swept since the previous internal sample, (F(cp) - F(cp0))/(cp - cp0) with the oracle's RazorCore.F; the midpoint below |cp - cp0| < 1e-7; the plain sample at blade entry. Half an internal sample of carrier-content lag, uncompensated (the engine header states why).

divergences.description: The onset lock (a note-start coupling burst, Kenv, decaying over dissolve) is BIPOLAR, the C++'s law (ADR-056): Kenv = 8*onset*|onset|, its positive part added to the sync target and 3x its negative part to the splay target (the x3 of the steady splay gain), so a negative onset is a SPLAY burst. SwarmSynth squares the sign away (Kenv = 8*onset^2), so onset -x played the same sync burst as +x, although the composed engine exposes onset -1..1. For onset >= 0 both laws are the same expressions (ADR-056's superset proof), so nothing there moves. Built as a text patch of SwarmSynth's noteOn and controlTick (the engine's SWARM_PATCHES); 0 is SwarmSynth's expression, character for character.

divergences.description: The blade's frame holds its course where the swarm's phase centre is undefined, and a member's lead reaches its blade as a ramp, never a step (ROADMAP B461; the human, 2026-10-12, heard a click inside one held note and saw it 'where the voices cross each other'). The oracle measures each member's lead from psi, the angle of the summed phase vectors, every 32 samples, and its render reads the lead at once; where the order parameter R passes through zero psi swings by up to half a cycle in one tick and every blade jumps. With the flag on each voice keeps a frame angle: every tick it advances by the members' mean phase advance (measured where the phases step, not predicted from the member frequencies, which the swarm moves every 16 samples), then moves toward psi by a fraction of the difference and by no more than 8 cycles per second (converted per tick from seconds). The fraction is g(R), rising linearly from 0 at R 0.05 to 1 at R 0.25, per REFERENCE tick of 32 samples at 48 kHz (1/1500 s); a tick of length dt takes 1 - (1 - g)^(dt / dtRef), so the frame closes on the centre in the same time at every sample rate, with g 0 giving 0 and g 1 giving 1 exactly. Where that correction is whole and inside the rate the frame is assigned psi itself, so in a locked swarm the leads' targets are the oracle's bit for bit. Each lead then travels to its value under the frame over the 32 samples of the tick, the shortest way round. A note's first tick sets the frame to psi and the leads outright (the oracle's law). A member that joins a held frame (N raised, or the flag turned on at a smaller N) has its lead set at the next tick, not ramped. Spread law 3 reads the lead under the frame, not its ramp: through spread(), as a step per tick, an exception to 'never as a step' that B460 owns. The three constants were set by ADR-216.

divergences.finding: (1) ACCEPTANCE 2 AS THE HUMAN RULED IT (2026-10-12, on the lead's recommendation: 'judge the fix with Position spread at 0, at both 1x and 2x oversampling. The present law must still read at least one jump there, so the test can see the fault. The pad-as-shipped row is printed but not judged, and becomes B460's test.'). With Position spread 0 the flag-on pad reads no isolated jump at C3, G3 or C4 at os 2 or at os 1, and the present law reads 3 / 1 / 2 and 5 / 2 / 4. The pad as shipped still reads 1 / 0 / 0 at os 2 and 3 / 0 / 0 at os 1 with the flag on: those are B460's steps (the residual above), and that row is B460's test. (2) After the frame has held through R near zero the measured centre is about half a cycle away, and the frame then turns to it at the rate limit: about 60 ms of every blade sweeping half a cycle, in place of the jump. (3) THE HALF-CYCLE TIE. Which way the frame turns on leaving a hold is the sign of its error there, and that error can sit on the half-cycle tie. At N 6 (the pad) it does not: the critic measured 12 exits with |error| 0.300 to 0.490 cycles, the least 0.00994 clear of the tie. At N 2 it always does: the summed phase vector lies on the two members' bisector, so every exit is half a cycle to within a rounding (measured: within 8.5e-15 of the tie on all 22 exits probed, either sign; the critic: 1e-16 to 4e-15), and the turn's direction is decided by that rounding. The C++ and the JS do not share sin, cos or atan2. Two N 2 parity rows were built and are HELD OUT of the committed scenario set until the human rules what the frame does after a crossing (ROADMAP B461): `C/D6 two members, detune 14` and `C/D6 two members, detune 30`, both the renderer's two-blade base (N 3, w 0.3, k 5.5, c 0.6, b2on 1, mode2 4, w2 0.2, k2 3, c2 0.35) with N 2, frame 1, phaseMode 2, law 0, driftRate 0.1, bspread 0.3, detune 14 (or 30), K 0.45, A 300, frameHold 1, snapped, seed 0xB385, 48 kHz, notes 45 and 52 at velocity 0.85 held for 900 blocks of 128 and released for 20. As written they hold parity (rms 2.8e-15 and 4.3e-15, max-abs 2.2e-13 and 2.8e-13, events identical); with the note frequencies moved 1 to 15 ULP on both sides (the renderer's --nudge) 2 of the 30 renders miss (detune 30 at 2 ULP: rms 2.7e-2, max-abs 0.61; detune 14 at 13 ULP: rms 2.8e-2, max-abs 0.64; events differ). They hold only where the two math libraries agree to the last bit, and CI's lanes run another one. No tie rule is built.

divergences.description: The feedback / cross-mod loop keeps the ORACLE'S TAP (the PolyBLEP output, render :840) and runs it through a one-pole low-pass at 5 kHz (LOOP_FC; a time constant in seconds, converted per internal sample). ADR-189 A1: the tap change first built (tapping the current sample) was DROPPED: it moved broad#828's rate-locked cycle from R/5 to R/3 instead of curing it, and made broad#857 A5 6.2 dB worse. Measured on broad#828 A1/E5 at os 1/2/4/8, the worst line over its local floor: off +19.4, 3 kHz +2.3, 4 kHz +1.3, 5 kHz +2.2, 6 kHz +3.4, 8 kHz +7.1; broad#540 (the other patch with the cycle): off +20.2, 4 kHz +1.6, 5 kHz +3.0. 5 kHz is the highest cutoff with every line within the +-3 dB scatter of a clean reference. Halving or quartering the loop gain leaves the cycle; os only moves it. The oracle's xin is overwritten in stepM before the blade step reads it.

divergences.description: The coupling smoother's per-tick coefficient comes from a time constant in SECONDS, B150's law in the C++ (SwarmCore(): 0.08 at 44.1 kHz exactly, else 1 - exp(-(16/sr)/kKsmTauSeconds), kKsmTauSeconds = 4.3512 ms, the value that gives 0.08 at 44.1 kHz), in place of SwarmSynth's literal 0.08 per 16-sample tick at every rate (an ADR-009 per-tick constant: 4.35 ms at 44.1 kHz, 4.00 ms at 48 kHz, 2.00 ms at 96 kHz). Resolved once per SwarmSynth, at construction, as the C++ does. 44.1 kHz is special-cased to the literal, as in the C++, because the round trip is three ULP short of 0.08. 48 kHz: 0.073746064208033535. divergences.description: The DEVICE default oversampling is os 1, and os 2 is the HQ setting. The SCALPEL oracle constructs at setOS(2), and the composed engine inherits that, so the product default now differs from the oracle's. It is a patch-default change, not an engine one: the SCALPEL lab's `DEF` is the oracle's constructor values with `LAB_DEF` written over them, and `LAB_DEF.os = 1` is the whole divergence. The engine core's setOS(2) (h2/engine/engine.h), every parity scenario and both self-digests stay at os 2, so no digest moves. Saved state is protected by its own `os` field (ADR-197 rule E): a record that carries `os` plays at it; a record with none (the factory presets, which the listening gate covered) plays at the new default. tools/labharness/os_default_check.mjs holds that and its must-fail controls.

divergences.description: A taken voice fades (ROADMAP B459; the human, 2026-10-12, first playtest of the preview: 'Breathing Pad is very clicky'). With the pool full a poly note-on takes a voice that is still sounding (ADR-083 tier 2, the quietest releasing tail, or tier 3, the oldest held voice; the same picks at a voice cap) and restarts it as a fresh voice: the envelope keeps its level while the phases, filters and DC state reset, so the output jumps in one sample. With the flag on, a picked voice that is active with its envelope at or above 1e-3 is not restarted. Its sound fades to zero over 0.005 s (a linear gain ramp on top of its own envelope, the cull's arithmetic, counted in whole samples: 240 at 48 kHz, 221 at 44.1 kHz), the note waits in the voice, and it starts from silence at the exact sample the ramp ends, as a note on a free voice starts. The render cuts itself at that sample, so the start does not depend on the host's block size. For the keep-phase snapshot a voice under a steal's fade counts as sounding for the fade's whole length, whether or not its own release floor ended it sooner, and at the sample the fade ends; so the snapshot a note reads during a fade or at its end is the one taken at that sample, from that voice if it is the newest (ADR-216 A3 item 5; what this does and does not guarantee is in finding 2). While a note waits its voice is the note's: it carries the note's age from the take, the live count and the cap count it, tiers 1 and 2 pass it by, a retune reaches it as it reaches a started note (the played frequency moves, the struck one stays the glide target), a panic or a mode change cancels it (the fade runs out), and if tier 3 picks the voice again the newer note replaces the waiting one without restarting the fade (ADR-216 A3 item 3). At a full cap with capPolicy 1, a waiting note that is the oldest held is cancelled and the new note takes the free slot. A voice already fading under the cull is taken over from its present gain, over the samples the cull had left or 0.005 s, whichever is shorter (ADR-216 A3 item 4). The samples the cull had left are ceil(cullG * (0.008 * sr)); cullG is 1 less a sum of rounded steps, and at 48 kHz that product stands about 2e-12 above a whole number, so the wait is the cull's remainder plus one sample (a tail culled 200 samples before waits 185). It is plain IEEE arithmetic with no libm call, the same in the JS. Mono and legato are untouched, and a voice below 1e-3 restarts at once as before. THE RULES OF A TAKEN VOICE ARE ADR-216 A3, PROPOSED BY THE LEAD FOR THE HUMAN TO RATIFY AT MERGE. They replace ADR-216's 'a note-off for the waiting note is remembered: the note starts, then releases at once' (measured: under that rule a note whose off came inside its wait was never heard, and the next note then took a HELD voice in its place): (a) A STOLEN NOTE IS LATE BY ITS WAIT IN EVERY RESPECT, ITS RELEASE INCLUDED (A3 item 1): a note that started W samples late has every note-off for it take effect W samples after it arrives, whether the off comes while the note still waits, on the sample it starts, or any time after, so it sounds for exactly as long as its key was held; a second off before the first takes effect changes nothing, and a panic, a mode change or a new take of the voice cancels a pending off; a note on a free voice has W 0 and is released at once, as before; (b) THE TIERS JUDGE A VOICE BY ITS KEY, NOT BY ITS DELAYED GATE (A3 item 2): a note whose key is up is a releasing tail to the tiers, whether it is still waiting to start (then it is the quietest: the next note takes its voice and replaces it, without restarting the fade) or is sounding out its late release (a tail at its own level), and held notes stay protected (ADR-083's point). Such a tail has its gate on for up to the fade's length. Taken by a note, its pending off goes with the rest of the old sound; restarted under the threshold, the restart clears it; picked by the cull, it is released there, at most 0.005 s before its off was due, so the cull's fade runs on a released voice, as it always has. At a full cap with capPolicy 1, the oldest HELD voice is judged by its key in the same way. The constant was set by ADR-216.

divergences.finding: (1) WHICH ROWS OF THE CHECK HAVE BLADE 2 OFF, AND WHY. The pad's second blade is a noise blade (mode2 3), which draws from the engine's shared random stream on every noise step while it renders; a note-on that starts a voice draws from the same stream. So a render with a chord and one without it hear different noise from the note-on onwards whenever the chord STARTS a voice there, taken voice or not, and a with/without comparison reads that as a jump. With the lead's seven settings and blade 2 on, a chord that takes NO voice read 2 % to 50 % depending on its notes and on the host seed (ROADMAP B459's row read 1 %), and one held note plus a note on a free voice read 0.007 % at C3 and 94 % at E3. So the free-voice control and every flag-off control are judged with blade 2 off (a free-voice start and a flag-off restart both draw at the note-on). A take draws nothing at the note-on, so the flag-on rows of a pool taken whole are judged with blade 2 on as well; the rows at pools 6 and 8 stay on the blade-2-off basis they were measured on, and their blade-2-on readings are printed unjudged on every run (chord 2, no voice taken: 50.3 %, and 17.4 % under spread law 4). (2) NOT CHASED: that noise blade's draws are themselves a way one note changes another's sound (every note-on re-seeds every other voice's noise from that sample on). It is not D7's. Nor is this, a fault of the engine with the flag off too: with keepPhase on, a note-on after full silence reads the snapshot left at the last host block boundary at which a voice still sounded (a voice with no fade on it that dies of its own release floor when nothing else sounds). A flag-on render that contains such a death carries it too, and D7 adds no dependence of its own. Measured 2026-10-13 on a keep-phase fuzz (3000 random scripts: releases of 5, 20 and 300 ms, pools of 1 to 3, half with panics, each rendered whole and chopped at 1 and at 16 frames): 524 scripts depend on the chop with the flag off and 435 with it on; 92 with the flag off only and 3 with it on only, each of the 3 containing such a death in its flag-on render (one laid out sample by sample: a voice released by a panic dies 36 samples before the next note-on, with nothing else sounding). With that window closed in a scratch copy of the engine, 0 of the 3000 depend, flag on or off. With the second critic's case put back in that copy (a voice that dies UNDER its ramp not counted for the snapshot), 1 of the 3000 does, with the flag on: the fuzz can see what D7 would add, and reads none. (3) Choices the ruling left open, accepted by the lead on 2026-10-13: the fade is counted in whole samples (round(0.005 * sr)); the old sound is released at the take; the waiting voice takes the note's age at the take and keeps it; notes whose fades end together start in the order they were struck; the fade runs its whole length even if the old voice's own release ends first; a fade outlives a cancelled wait; capPolicy 1 cancels a waiting note that is the oldest held; a polyMode change cancels every waiting note; the keep-phase snapshot is taken at a fade's end from the voice that just ended (the lead's reading, extended to a fade nobody waits on, and after the second critic's read to the whole length of a fade whose voice died sooner). The rules in the description are ADR-216 A3, PROPOSED, and the human's to ratify. (4) RULE (a) WAS BUILT TWICE. First as 'a stolen note keeps its gate, and an off that comes after the note has started is an ordinary off': that had a step, measured (an off 239 samples after the take kept a gate of 239 samples; one at 240 or 241 left a gate of 0 or 1 sample), and a stolen note held longer than the fade lost the fade's length of its gate. The lead replaced it on 2026-10-13 with the rule above, which has no step: the price is that a stolen note is released 0.005 s after its key. A note struck and released at the same instant on a taken voice has a gate of 0 and is silent (it starts from silence and is released at once); with the flag off it is heard, because the restarted voice keeps the old envelope's level (ADR-216 A3 item 6). RULE (b) WAS BUILT TWICE TOO. First with a late note that had started, and whose off had arrived but not yet taken effect, still HELD to the tiers (its gate is on). Measured by a second independent critic: a chord of two held at a pool of 3 under a back-to-back line (each line note struck 0 or 96 samples after the last one's release, as a sequencer sends them) lost a chord note at six of the eight line notes, where the flag off lost none; and at a pool of 2 with 45 and 52 held, a note released 96 samples after its take and the next struck 236, 244, 264 and 340 samples after it left 52 held, lost, lost and held: a step. The lead replaced it on 2026-10-13 with rule (b). On this build the line loses no chord note at 0, 96, 240 and 480 samples, 52 is held at all eight of the critic's timings, and a stuck-note fuzz of 1500 random scripts (takes, late offs, retunes, panics, cap and mode changes, the flag toggled) reads 0 violations and 0 notes stuck at the end. (5) THE LEDGER CHECK COULD NOT HEAR THIS DIVERGENCE: its fixed script strikes both notes at sample 0 into an empty pool, where no voice can be taken. ROADMAP B465 gave its scenarios a note script, which this entry's two scripted scenarios use.

divergences.description: The member spread values reach the blades as ramps, never as steps (ROADMAP B460; the lead, 2026-10-12, measuring B459: 'the spread law steps the sound every 32 samples'). The oracle recomputes every member's spread values once per 32-sample tick (spread(), spreadMember()) and its render reads them every sample, so each tick's change arrives in one sample; under the drift law (law 4) that is a random step of every blade's position 1500 times a second. With the flag on, at each tick every value a blade reads travels from where it stands to the law's new value in 32 equal steps: one at the tick, the rest at the end of each sample for the next (ADR-216 A1 item 6, as D6's lead), so it arrives on the tick's last sample. The length is the engine's own tick; no other constant is involved. THE VALUES (eighteen: nine per blade). Ramped linearly: rotation rate (rotOff), width (wMul), depth (dAdd), index (iMul), the sine->saw band-limit's r (mr), of both blades, and cut (kAdd, kMul) while Quantize is off. Ramped the shortest way round: position (cOff, cOff2), which a blade reads modulo one cycle; the value it starts from is first moved by whole cycles onto the target's branch, which no blade can hear. Ramped as a matched pair with r: the band-limit's normaliser (mn), which is asin(r); where r is at or under the law's threshold (1e-4) the law writes 1, the wave is a plain sine and reads no normaliser, and the ramp's target is r itself, asin's own limit, because a ramp between 1 and asin(r) would silence the member on the way. Set, not ramped: cut under Quantize (kq), which the law itself steps (a whole-number offset, or a slot of the rule's list). Not touched: mor and kEff, which no blade reads. WHO IS SET INSTEAD OF RAMPED (ADR-216 A1 item 4's rule for a lead, applied here): every value at a note's first spread() and at the first after the flag turns on; a member that has just joined (N raised); a member still waiting on onset scatter, which is silent and holds the law's own values until the first tick after it starts. A note-on's spread() on a voice already sounding (a mono retrigger) is not a tick: the law runs, so its draws keep their order, and the ramps stay as they stand. Spread law 3 reads each member's lead (the lead under D6's frame when D6 holds one), and its values ramp like any other law's: that is how the lead reaches the blade as a ramp through spread() (ADR-216 A1 item 5, the exception D6 left to B460). EVERY RULE IN THIS PARAGRAPH BEYOND 'the values ramp across the tick' IS PROPOSED, the human's to ratify: the records give no more.

metric.detector: tools/h2_spread_ramp_check.mjs (./verify full), on the C++ engine through the harness: one held note of ledger/breathing-pad AS SHIPPED (no patch setting written over it; frameHold 1 and stealFade 0 pinned), 8 s, 48 kHz, host seeds 1 to 8, at C3, G3 and C4, at os 2 and os 1 (48 renders a row). An isolated jump is tools/h2_frame_hold_check.mjs's (a sample step on the left pre-limiter bus over 0.02 and over 3 times the 99th percentile of the steps in the surrounding 100 ms). JUDGED, as the lead ruled (PROPOSED, ADR-216 A4, the human's to ratify): (i) on the pad as shipped, flag on, no isolated jump AT A TICK BOUNDARY; (ii) on its twin with the noise blade silent (depth2 0: still evaluated, so the random stream and the spread's walk are untouched), flag on, no isolated jump at all. The pad's whole count is printed with each remaining jump attributed, and is not judged. A tick boundary is the tick positions a step of the law can reach, derived in the check's header from the engine's code: positions 0 and 1 at os 1 (the blade's output is one internal step late; a PolyBLEP's leading half lands one earlier), positions 0 to 6 at os 2 (every position at which the decimation filter moves by at least 1 % of its largest move for a step entering at either internal step of the tick's sample). The tick measure is B460's own, as that check defines it: the second difference's mean square per position in the 32-sample tick, the largest of the first four positions over the median of all 32, in dB

divergences.finding: (1) ROADMAP B460'S FIRST ADDED ACCEPTANCE IS NOT MET AT OS 1, AND WHAT IS JUDGED INSTEAD IS PROPOSED (ADR-216 A4).
